clue.text: Artist shows impertinence after tea

indicators.note: after puts the impertinence piece behind the tea piece

parts.note: cha is an old slang word for tea
gall means cheek or brazen impudence

explanation.surface: A painter is cheeky to people once tea has been served.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a Russian-French painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Protect theologian imprisoned by old king

indicators.note: imprisoned by means locked inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
DD is a Doctor of Divinity, a theologian

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch jails a theologian to shield him.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is a British nursery-rhyme king.
explanation.definitionFit: To pamper and overprotect someone is a fair synonym for protect.

clue.text: Beg a copper to ring

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny, a copper coin
to peal is to ring, as bells do

explanation.surface: Pleading with a policeman to phone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a policeman but is a penny coin, P.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an earnest request is a synonym for beg.

clue.text: Under terrible strain, fellow is bitter

indicators.note: Under places the fellow below the jumbled letters in this down entry
terrible means in a bad state, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman or fellow

explanation.surface: A man under heavy stress turns sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges STRAIN to ASTRIN; 'Under' puts GENT beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, harsh taste or manner is a synonym for bitter.

clue.text: Being prone to dishonesty

explanation.surface: Having a tendency to be untruthful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prone to' reads as 'inclined to'; here 'Being prone' is one definition and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Recumbent is one sense; telling falsehoods is the other.

clue.text: It could give one a bad head

definitions.text: It could give one a bad head

parts.words: It could give one a bad head
parts.note: read as a bad head, ILL plus NESS, a ness being a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: Something that might leave you with a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: Cryptically a 'bad head' is ILL (bad) plus NESS, a headland, as in Orford Ness on the Suffolk coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickness of any kind can bring on a sore head, so the plain reading is fair too.

clue.text: Isn't train moving? It's on it's way!

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger asks whether the train is going, and is told it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something travelling between places is on its way, an idiom.

clue.text: One embraced by boy is placed horizontally

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a lad is a boy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone hugged by a youth is lying down.
explanation.definitionFit: Put down flat, as a carpet or table is, a synonym.

clue.text: Plague is half the content of a poem

indicators.note: the content of means what is held inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem
demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: A grim plague takes up half of a poem's subject matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' gives DEMI rather than halving anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A widespread outbreak of disease is a synonym for plague.

clue.text: It is insane to make something acceptable?

indicators.note: in places the first words inside the last one

explanation.surface: Is it crazy to clean things up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'insane' must be split as 'in sane': IT IS goes inside SANE.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove offensive parts so something is palatable is a synonym, a censoring sense.

clue.text: Mark stores record in warehouse

indicators.note: stores means holds inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a dot is a small mark
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark keeps a record in a storage building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name but is the word for a spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storage building, a synonym for a warehouse.

clue.text: Sixth sense needed in schooling

parts.note: tuition is teaching or schooling

explanation.surface: Claims that a sixth sense has to be taught at school.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth sense is knowing something without reasoning, which is a synonym for instinctive insight.

clue.text: Star puts bullets into FBI agent

parts.note: bullets are made of lead, so lead stands for them
into gives the short word in
a G-man is American slang for an FBI agent (government man)

explanation.surface: A film star fires bullets into a federal agent, an action-movie scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puts' is only a link; 'into' is not a container signal but supplies IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a film or play is its principal male actor, the hero's role.

clue.text: Paddy harbours small annoyance

indicators.note: harbours means shelters within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of temper, as is a pet

explanation.surface: An Irishman named Paddy nurses a minor irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like a name but is a tantrum; 'in a pet' means in a sulk or huff.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuisance that bothers you is a synonym for a small annoyance.

clue.text: Outline for renovated hotel suite

indicators.note: renovated means rebuilt, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plans for a refurbished set of hotel rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark shape seen against light is an outline, a synonym.

clue.text: Happy mood obtained through strong drink

definitions.meaning: being cheerful and in high spirits
fine liquor such as whisky or gin, read as quality spirits

explanation.surface: Cheerfulness that comes from drinking hard liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerfulness is the idiom; read literally the phrase is fine liquor.

clue.text: Extrovert's expenditure

definitions.meaning: read as an extrovert is, that is sociable and friendly
a plural noun for money spent, plural where the clue word is singular

explanation.surface: How much a sociable person spends.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociable describes an extrovert; spending of money is the other sense.

clue.text: Stole whizz for a notorious gangster

parts.note: a stole is a scarf worn round the shoulders
a whizz is an expert, an ace

explanation.surface: Someone took an expert to catch a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' looks like a verb but is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the nickname of Al Capone, the Chicago crime boss.

clue.text: Show approval of operative on strike

indicators.note: on places the operative piece above the strike piece in this down entry

parts.note: a hand is a worker or operative
to clap is to strike, as of hands

explanation.surface: Backing a factory worker who has walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on strike' suggests industrial action, but 'strike' means hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause is a display of approval, read as a noun phrase 'show (of) approval'.

clue.text: Fastens shirt with irritation? It's a feature of the fabric!

parts.note: chains means fastens or secures
T stands for a T-shirt
an itch is an irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: An itchy shirt fastened up, blamed on the material.
explanation.definitionFit: This looped stitch is used in embroidery and knitting, so it is part of a fabric's make-up.

clue.text: In business one gets criticism

indicators.note: In puts the one inside the business word

parts.note: trade means business or commerce
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: In commerce, everyone faces disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: An angry, long speech of censure is a synonym for criticism.

clue.text: Soldier is unable to withdraw

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
can't means is unable

explanation.surface: A soldier cannot pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement is the verb sense of withdraw.

clue.text: Daughter's about to regret being unpleasant

indicators.note: about here means surrounded by, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: rue means regret

explanation.surface: A daughter is going to be sorry for being nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'going to'; in fact 'Daughter's about' means D is surrounded, and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Impolite and offensive behaviour is a synonym for unpleasant.

clue.text: Vice-consul managed to be emphatic

indicators.note: managed means handled or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A diplomat got by in a forceful way.
explanation.definitionFit: Decisive and beyond doubt, a fair synonym for emphatic, as in an emphatic victory.

clue.text: Shoddy cold store

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a heap is a store or pile

explanation.surface: A poor-quality refrigerated warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Of low quality and badly made is a synonym for shoddy.

clue.text: Precious part of a perfect weekend

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A precious portion of a perfect couple of days off.
explanation.definitionFit: Affectedly dainty or quaint is the sense precious has when meaning overly refined.

clue.text: Financial support for a new local development

indicators.note: development means building up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Funding for a new housing development in the area.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular sum of money given to someone is financial support, a synonym.

clue.text: Headdress is first-class in design, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection means seen in a mirror, so the letters are read backwards
in places the first-class letters inside the design word

parts.note: art is design or creative work
A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: A coronet is top-quality in its design when you think it over.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 for first-class is written AI here; 'on reflection' turns the assembled ARAIT round.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled crown worn on the head is a type of headdress.

clue.text: Squeeze out of train

definitions.meaning: to press juice or liquid from something
a fast train making few stops

explanation.surface: Someone pushed off a train.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing out juice is one sense; a fast train is another.

clue.text: It is given here

explanation.surface: A statement of fact, as if a premise is granted.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift is something given; being in attendance means being here.
